data.why: app.py takes all inputs from sidebar sliders/selectboxes and computes everything in-memory via mars_os.circadian_kernel; it never reads a file or connects to db/schema.sql, so no example or synthetic data is needed.

goals: Set a mission duration and current sol, then read off today's accumulated circadian drift (hours) and cognitive Performance Index
Toggle crew chronotype (morning/intermediate/evening) and wake time to see how individual phase preference shifts the drift and alert level
Dial phototherapy correction factor from 0% to 100% and observe how much it suppresses drift accumulation and shifts the GREEN/YELLOW/RED sol distribution over the mission
Compare the four built-in intervention scenarios (none, 30%, 60%, full phototherapy) side by side on performance and drift curves to decide on an operational correction target
Read the prescribed 480nm light therapy window (start/end time, duration, lux, phase-advance vs delay direction) for the current sol and correction setting
Export the full per-sol mission timeseries and the sampled timeline table as CSV for offline analysis

review.summary: The tree describes the dashboard accurately: three sensible phases, seven tasks that are neither too coarse nor too fine, specific labels that match the UI, and 11 sampled screens that all show what their nodes claim. Before filing, it needs the t3 and goal wording toned down (PI cycles, so more correction does not reliably improve status), a note that the four comparison curves ignore chronotype and correction, a fix to the misleading context on the sol-106 action, and DELAY recorded as unreachable by construction.
